articles.title: Nicholas Galitzine Eyeing Ichabod Crane Role In Sony’s ‘Hollow’ Starring Sydney Sweeney
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Halloween season may be over, but Sony Pictures isn’t done adding to its already stacked cast for another spooky feature. Sources tell Deadline that Nicholas Galitzine is in final negotiations to play Ichabod Crane in Hollow opposite Sydney Sweeney . The film also stars Belmont Cameli and is based on filmmaker Lindsey Anderson Beer’s forthcoming debut novel. Beer is attached to direct as well as adapt her novel, which will be published by Putnam, an imprint of Penguin Random House, in fall 2027. The novel sold in a competitive situation and will be globally translated at launch. Beer and her Lab Brew banner are producing Hollow , as will Sweeney via her Honey Trap banner and LuckyChap; Hollow marks the first film as producer for Honey Trap, the newly launched company that has Kaylee McGregor serving as President of Production and Development. It recently announced a first-look deal with Sony Pictures. Beer’s novel is a reimagining of The Legend of Sleepy Hollow , told through the perspective of Katrina Van Tassel, played by Sweeney. Reframing one of literature’s most iconic heroines, the novel positions Van Tassel not as a romantic prize but as the central figure in a dangerous mystery and seductive supernatural love triangle. The story blends gothic atmosphere, psychological intrigue and erotic thriller elements into a contemporary, high-concept reinvention of the tale. Crane was famously played by Johnny Depp in Tim Burton’s 1999 adaptation Sleepy Hollow , Galitzine now gets his shot at giving a new spin to the classic character in a role that had a long list of actors chasing the part. Following his breakout role in the Amazon pic Red, White & Royal Blue, Galitzine has been one of the busiest and more sought-after rising stars in town. articles.title: New York Times In Advanced Talks To Buy Letterboxd For Reported $330 Million
articles.content: The New York Times Company is in advanced talks to acquire the beloved cinephile social media platform Letterboxd , Deadline has confirmed. The only other remaining bidder, A24, is out of the running. The New York Times first reported that its parent is in pole position to buy the site from Canadian hedge fund Tiny, pegging the deal at $330 million. The field was initially said to include Netflix, Sony, the former Paramount and others but most fell away as the price rose. Another suitor, a nonprofit called Intrinsic Entertainment , told Deadline tonight that it’s assembled a group of like-minded investors and was several weeks away from making a $300 million offer. Related Stories News Rider Strong Stopped Rating Films On Letterboxd "For The Sake Of My Career": "Not A Good Look" News As Letterboxd Draws Interest From The New York Times, A24 And More, One Of Its Bankers Calls It "A Phenomenon" It isn’t not clear if the NYT bid includes the stakes of Letterboxd founders Matthew Buchanan and Karl von Randow, CEO and CTO, who each own 20% of the company after selling 60% to Tiny in 2023. Letterboxd said in a statement at the start of Tiny’s sale process that the duo, who are based in New Zealand, would be involved in any decision about Letterboxd’s future. Watch on Deadline The report today said the NYT is considering leaving the duo at the helm. A24 had promised Letterboxd independence and to leave its business model unchanged. Tiny had hired boutique investment bank LionTree to oversee the sale process. Reps from LionTree, Letterboxd, the New York Times and A24 didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. Speaking at an FT conference recently, Alex Michael, a LionTree senior managing director, raved about Letterboxd, calling it “a phenomenon” that attracts 30 million monthly users “with zero paid marketing.”

articles.content: UPDATED, with final numbers: NBC News ‘ midterm Election Night coverage topped major networks, drawing an average of 6.7 million viewers in primetime Tuesday, according to the final figures from Nielsen. We understand he has temporarily been dropped from shows including James Corden and Ruth Jones’ new Apple TV series The Choir , the third season of the BBC ’s Such Brave Girls and another new BBC show, Push. Bayles told Deadline he is “appalled and sickened by Brand’s actions” but couldn’t recall the incident. He said he stopped working with Brand in 2010, has not had contact with him since and complaints about Brand’s behavior were never made to him at the time. articles.content: Nearly a year after she went missing, LAPD has arrested two people in connection to the death of Christina Downer, the late sister of Saturday Night Live writer Jimmy Fowlie . On Thursday, officers took 41-year-old Delorean Bijon Brandon, who is believed to be Downer’s boyfriend, and Kaylee Markowski, 34, into custody for allegedly murdering and disposing of her body, before concealing their involvement. Brandon and Markowski are both being held at Metropolitan Detention Center, where they have been booked on suspicion of murder and are both being held on $2 million bail. Watch on Deadline Downer’s family reported her missing on Dec. 18, 2025, following a welfare check requested by her ex-husband after he hadn’t heard from her in an extended period of time. Detectives with LAPD’s Robbery-Homicide Division took over the investigation when her cellphone was discovered washed ashore on a Santa Monica beach. Last December, Fowlie sought help from friends and followers as he searched Downer’s Koreatown neighborhood, noting they were “worried that she isn’t safe.” Fowlie announced in April that LAPD had informed the family that Downer was “ no longer alive ,” and were treating the case as a homicide. articles.title: Gay Influencer Famed for Dancing in High Heels Faces Middle Age in Nine-Year Taiwan Creative Content Fest Documentary ‘My Silly Flirty Boys’
articles.content: A gay influencer in Taiwan who became famous dancing in high heels, and the filmmaker who trained his camera on him for nine years, both stare down middle age in “ My Silly Flirty Boys .” The documentary from Taiwan-based Hong Kong filmmaker Frankie Sin is at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei. Sin followed Fufu from 2017 to 2026. Over that stretch, Fufu built a following with racy dance routines, performances in high heels and his online channel “FJ234,” where he talked openly about desire and helped bring drag queens and other LGBTQ+ performers to mainstream audiences. Not everyone approved. More than 10 years ago, Sin swapped one of Hong Kong’s conservative outlying islands for Taiwan, hoping its reputation for openness would give him a place to belong. articles.title: The Weeknd Breaks Record for Highest-Grossing Tour by a Male Artist With $1.3 Billion
articles.content: The Weeknd has broken the record for the highest-grossing tour by a male artist in history as his “After Hours Til Dawn” stadium tour wrapped with a final performance at TM Stadium National in Kuala Lumpur, bringing the final gross to over $1.3 billion. articles.content: Jalen Brunson , who led the New York Knicks to their first NBA championship in 53 years in June, guest starred as a cop in Thursday’s episode of “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.” He appears in the episode for one brief scene, meeting up with Mariska Hargitay ‘s Olivia Benson to provide information on a suspect he’d had a run-in with in the past. articles.title: Helene Hahn Loyd, Former Disney and DreamWorks SKG Exec, Dies at 78
articles.summary: Loyd died peacefully in her sleep on Oct. 24, in Park City, Utah.
articles.content: Helene Hahn Loyd, the former Disney evp and one of the original executives at DreamWorks SKG , has died. She was 78. She was born in Westbury, New York, and graduated from Hofstra University in 1970. After graduating, she moved to Los Angeles and began temporarily working at Paramount Pictures while attending law school. She subsequently earned her degree from Loyola Law School in 1975. Loyd would rejoin Paramount Pictures in 1997 and became senior vice president. She would go on to work at Walt Disney Studios, being named executive vice president in 1981, elevating her among the highest level of women working in the film business. Working with Jeffrey Katzenberg , Loyd was a key player in Disney’s renaissance, playing a hand in the company’s partnership with Pixar. Related Stories TV Shari Rosenblum, Disney TV Studios' PR Lead, Exits the Company TV Kimmarie Johnson, 'Beverly Hills, 90210' Actress, Dies at 50 She was recruited as one of the first executives to build DreamWorks SKG in 1994, which was founded by Katzenberg, Steven Spielberg and David Geffen. There, Loyd worked her way up to chief operating officer. During the duration of her career, Loyd served as a mentor to many upcoming female executives. Loyd left DreamWorks in 2004, moving to Park City and taking on skiing as a passion. The executive’s husband of over two decades, Charles “Chuck” Loyd Jr., died in July. The family has asked those who wish to make a donation in their memory to donate to U.S. Ski & Snowboard, honoring their shared love of skiing and their commitment to supporting the next generation of athletes.

articles.title: Hollywood Quietly Banning Prediction Market Betting on Movie News, Release Dates (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Employees at studios and production companies are being warned against profiting off their knowledge of insider information. But experts say there's almost no way to stop it.
articles.content: If you’re an industry insider tempted to drop a few thousand on Kalshi predicting who will be cast as the next James Bond, think again. The Hollywood Reporter has learned studios and production companies have been quietly issuing new guidelines to employees warning them not to engage in prediction market betting. The warnings prohibit employees from placing bets on news events like studio earnings, casting, or even release dates. Passing information along to friends and family for them to place bets is likewise forbidden. At least one company set up a hotline where staffers can anonymously report on their fellow employees suspected of placing bets. In a way, such updates are an expansion on longstanding rules which forbid employees from insider trading in the stock market. And many instances of prediction market profiteering using insider corporate information might violate federal law already. But with prediction markets allowing betting on everything from who will be cast as the next Wonder Woman to who will be eliminated on Dancing with the Stars , the opportunities for stealthily cashing in on insider knowledge has dramatically increased. “You now have, essentially, an explosion in the number of employers who have to think about insider trading rules from an ethical standpoint,” says Joshua Mitts, a law professor at Columbia University who has extensively studied the legalities and trends surrounding prediction market betting. “And totally apart from the question of criminal prosecution, is just the compliance problem — educating your employees on what’s allowed.” THR’s parent company, PMC, which also owns Dick Clark Productions and other publications such as Variety and Deadline , has likewise updated its employee handbook to ban prediction market betting in recent weeks. articles.title: Kimmarie Johnson, ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’ Actress, Dies at 50
articles.summary: She was a former Miss Pennsylvania USA winner, which led her to compete in the 1993 Miss USA beauty pageant, where she placed in the top six.
articles.content: Kimmarie Johnson, the Beverly Hills, 90210 actress who also competed in the 1993 Miss USA beauty pageant, has died. She was 50. Johnson died Wednesday after experiencing a “heart event” at her Los Angeles home on Oct. 27, her niece Rhonda Scott told People . She was taken to Cedars-Sinai Medical Center and diagnosed with a “heart aneurysm condition.” “She radiated a light so strong and bright,” said Scott. “People who came in contact with her felt nothing but positive energy. We will miss her tremendously and will continue to honor her life forever.” Related Stories Movies Charles F. Porter, Actor and 'Finding Faith' Producer, Dies at 47 TV Tori Spelling, Brian Austin Green Go Vertical in Scripted Microdrama Johnson was featured on a 1998 episode of Beverly Hills, 90210 , where she portrayed the character of Judy. Before beginning her career as an actress in 1998, she worked as a flight attendant and went on to sign with the modeling agency Docherty. She competed in the 1992 Miss Pennsylvania USA pageant, which she won with no history as a beauty queen. Her victory led her to compete in the 1993 Miss USA beauty pageant, where she placed in the top six. In 1996, Johnson moved out to L.A. and continued to model while also expanding her career into acting. Her first credit came in 1998 with Troy Byer’s drama Let’s Talk About Sex . The actress went on to appear in projects including Dude, Where’s My Car? , Shadow Fury , Wanda at Large , Break a Leg and Tucker War’s . Johnson had a son, Cameron Nino, in 2003, which led her to take a break from acting. During that time, she took classes at The Groundlings.

articles.title: Streaming Ratings: ‘From’ Netflix Effects Its Way to Top of the Charts
articles.content: Horror/sci-fi series From has developed a cult following on MGM+ over four seasons. That following got considerably larger in late October. Netflix added the first three seasons of From to its catalog on Oct. 19, and the show zoomed to the top of Nielsen’s streaming charts for the week. It scored 1.65 billion minutes of viewing, the largest weekly total for any acquired series in 2026. The Diplomat came in second overall — and first among original series — with 1.19 billion minutes of watch time. The political thriller grew by about 21 percent from 983 million minutes the previous week , when its fourth season premiered on Netflix. Prime Video’s The Terminal List returned to the charts with its second season premiere. The series delivered 830 million viewing minutes to place second among original shows ahead of Peacock’s Crystal Lake , which edged up to 790 million minutes (from 774 million) in its second week. Nobody Wants This began its third season on Netflix with 725 million viewing minutes, down by 20 percent from season two’s premiere week last year. Marvel series VisionQuest (490 million on Disney+) made its chart debut with the release of its third and fourth episodes, and Tulsa King (484 million on Paramount+) returned a week into its fourth season. The prior week’s top two shows, Below and Carrie , both fell out of the overall top 10 in their third weeks but remained on the original series chart. Carrie recorded 609 million minutes of viewing on Prime Video, and Below added 441 million on Netflix. The streaming premiere of Disney’s live-action Moana led the movie top 10 with 579 million minutes. Several Halloween-related films also made the rankings. Nielsen’s streaming ratings cover viewing on TV sets only and don’t include minutes watched on computers or mobile devices. The ratings only measure U.S. audiences. All told, primetime election coverage averaged 31.21 million viewers across 13 broadcast and cable outlets (the others were Telemundo, Univision, PBS, CNN en Espanol, Fox Business, Newsmax and NewsNation) . articles.title: Helene Hahn Loyd, Founding DreamWorks Exec and Influential Jeffrey Katzenberg Adviser, Dies at 78
articles.summary: Reaching the echelons of female executives in Hollywood at the time of her tenure, Loyd left the industry in 2004 The post Helene Hahn Loyd, Founding DreamWorks Exec and Influential Jeffrey Katzenberg Adviser, Dies at 78 appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: Reaching the echelons of female executives in Hollywood at the time of her tenure, Loyd left the industry in 2004 Helene Hahn Loyd, a senior executive who helped lead Walt Disney Studios through its renaissance in the 1980s and 1990s before joining the founding leadership team at DreamWorks SKG, died Oct. 24 at her Park City, Utah, home. She was 78. Loyd was among the highest-ranking women in the film industry during her tenure at Disney, where she was named executive vice president in 1981. Working alongside Jeffrey Katzenberg, she helped guide the studio’s resurgence, including its landmark partnership with Pixar. In 1994, Loyd was among the first executives recruited to build DreamWorks SKG, the studio founded by Steven Spielberg, Katzenberg and David Geffen. She eventually served as the company’s chief operating officer. Born Helene Burlakoff on July 13, 1948, in Westbury, New York, she was the youngest of three children. She graduated from Hofstra University in 1970 and moved to Los Angeles, where she took a temporary job at Paramount Pictures while attending law school. She earned her degree from Loyola Law School in 1975. Loyd rejoined Paramount in 1977 and rose to senior vice president, establishing a reputation as a formidable dealmaker. Throughout her career, she also mentored up-and-coming female executives, many of whom went on to become leaders in their fields. After leaving DreamWorks in 2004, Loyd settled in Park City, where she pursued skiing with the same intensity she brought to her work in Hollywood. In their memory, the family has requested donations to U.S. Ski & Snowboard, reflecting the couple’s shared love of skiing and support for the next generation of athletes.

articles.content: The new banner led by Luke Maxwell and Will Rowbotham will produce new films, television series and digital content Lionsgate and 3 Arts Entertainment are teaming up to launch a new production banner called Render Road. The idea is that the new venture will develop projects for a wide array of platforms – developing, producing and financing films and television series, along with digital storytelling and beyond. Render Road will collaborate with emerging voices alongside established artists, both on its own projects and in collaboration with other studios and production companies. The intention is to allow Lionsgate & 3 Arts to reach audiences in the places where they’re discovering and engaging with the horror genre. Partners Luke Maxwell and Will Rowbotham will spearhead the effort for 3 Arts. 3 Arts has helped cultivate a new generation of horror storytellers, with Kane Parsons (“Backrooms”), Ian Tuason (“Undertone,” the new “Paranormal Activity”) and Dylan Clark, who is directing the new “Blair Witch” for Lionsgate and Blumhouse Atomic and “Portrait of God” for Lionsgate and producers Sam Raimi and Jordan Peele. Horror is a key part of Lionsgate’s history – from “The Blair Witch Project” (part of their Artisan acquisition) to Eli Roth’s “Hostel” to the long-running “Saw” franchise. Among other projects, they have a remake of “Magic,” the classic 1978 film written by William Goldman, on the horizon, directed by Raimi and written by his “Send Help” collaborators Mark Swift and Damian Shannon. They also have “Portrait of God” and the new “Blair Witch” on the way, along with a new “Saw,” directed by Mike P. Nelson. 2026 has largely been defined by the breakout horror sensations, like A24’s “Backrooms” and Focus Features’ “Obsession,” which not only were massive hits at the global box office but encouraged younger moviegoers to get back to the movie theater. It makes sense that other studios are chasing the same audience – and the same level of engagement.

Searchlight Pictures will release it in theaters on Friday, November 6. ] Another melancholically splenetic Martin McDonagh jag about a banter-mad pair of murderers who go on a boys trip to purgatory (where they search their souls as they wait for death to find them), the prickly but unconvincing “ Wild Horse Nine ” strains to translate the post-Guy Ritchie bark of “In Bruges” into the language of a classic American Western. In this case, an American Western set on Easter Island and backdropped by Augusto Pinochet’s rise to power in the fall of 1973. But that decision is a double-edged sword that cuts the film off at the knees. Where “ In Bruges ” kicked off with the killing of a fictional altar boy, “Wild Horse Nine” is overshadowed by the deaths of thousands upon thousands of very real people, and that reality bleeds into the edges of the frame even when the seriocomic absurdity of McDonagh’s writing demands a world of pure invention. articles.summary: Indie Spirit and Gotham Award nominee Anna Lambe shines even brighter in a second season that sees her single mom double down on "leveling up" — at work, in love, and as a contributing member of her cherished Inuk community, which, like her, needs all the help it can get.
articles.content: There are dozens of scenes that capture “North of North’s” digestible, defiant kindness, but my favorite arrives near the start of the second season’s second episode. Siaja ( Anna Lambe ) wakes up, grabs a glass of water, and promptly spits it out. The local water supply is contaminated (“They must’ve cranked those chemicals again,” her mom says), so Siaja heads to the nearest store to load up on jugs of clean water. Outside, there’s an elderly woman perched on her snowmobile, smoking a cigarette, who loudly hassles Siaja for a little charity. “Must be nice,” the woman shouts, getting Siaja’s attention. “[You] buying filtered water. It’s too expensive [for me]. [I] gotta drink government pool water. Back in the day, we had nice ice straight from the river. Pure, nice, and healthy.” Related Stories ‘Hen’ Review: A Cockeyed Comedy Sees Europe’s Migrant Crisis Through the Eyes of a Chicken ‘Black Doves’ Review: Season 2 Sticks to Its Guns in Keira Knightley’s Excellent, Existential Spy Thriller On that last word, “healthy,” the woman takes a drag from her cigarette, and while she’s doubled over coughing, Siaja takes her forceful hint and puts one of her water jugs in the woman’s cart. “Here, you take this,” Siaja says. The woman, speaking in Inuktitut, does not say “thank you”; she asks if she can keep the jug. Then she hacks a loogie into the snow as Siaja drives off, punctuating just how little the gesture means to her. Now, it’s clear this woman knows exactly what she’s doing. She didn’t end up outside the town’s only source for clean water by accident, and Siaja knows it. But she also knows the woman is telling the truth: She’s too old to get ice for herself, and she’s too poor to afford purified water. Siaja also knows this woman is her elder, and elders should be taken care of. articles.summary: Executive-produced by Ari Aster, György Pálfi's new film evokes "EO" and "Flow" with its animal POV on humanity's moral failures.
articles.content: Among the bleakest films ever made, Werner Herzog’s “Stroszek” (1977) famously ends not with the suicide of its title character, but with a haunting coda in which a chicken pecks at a miniature piano inside a surreal roadside tourist trap’s coin-operated display. It’s a visual metaphor for the inescapable banality of life on Earth, and for the dehumanizing work people are forced to do to disguise the many failures of the American Dream. It’s also the last thing that Joy Division frontman Ian Curtis saw before he killed himself. “Look into the eyes of a chicken,” Herzog has said, “and you will see real stupidity. It is a kind of bottomless stupidity, a fiending stupidity. They are the most horrifying, cannibalistic, and nightmarish creatures in the world.” Related Stories Robert Pattinson to Receive 2026 American Cinematheque Award AI Movie ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Gets Serious with AI-Generated Grimes Cameo, Times Square Marketing Push, Oscar Screenings That sentiment has long endured as modern cinema’s definitive stance on chickens ( despite Aardman’s best efforts ), but now, after witnessing the 50 years of entropy that followed “Stroszek,” Hungarian filmmaker György Pálfi is crying fowl. Chickens are not the most horrifying, cannibalistic, and nightmarish creatures in the world, he contends. We are. How can you tell? Easy: Just look at us through the eyes of a chicken. A cute, cockeyed yarn that unspools like a feathered cross between “EO” and “Flow,” Pálfi’s “ Hen ” tells the story of a jet-black Leghorn chicken who escapes a Greek factory farm after she’s plucked from the rest of her flock because of the color of her plumage. articles.title: Robert Pattinson to Receive 2026 American Cinematheque Award
articles.summary: The prolific star of several successful 2026 films, from "The Odyssey" to "Primetime," will be the 40th recipient of the award from American Cinematheque after Ryan Gosling backed out of the event in October.
articles.content: The American Cinematheque Awards Gala is officially back on with actor Robert Pattinson , star of several films from 2026, from “Primetime” and “The Drama,” to “The Odyssey” and “Dune: Part Three,” as the 40th recipient. The milestone celebration will now take place on Tuesday, February 9, 2027, at The Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills. Previously, the 2026 edition of the fundraiser had been set for November 2 , with “Project Hail Mary” star Ryan Gosling accepting the award, but the incoming Marvel Cinematic Universe actor had to drop out of the event a month before due to a scheduling conflict. Now, prolific actor Pattinson will be the one to join a roster of honorees that include filmmakers and performers like Eddie Murphy, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, Denzel Washington, Nicole Kidman, George Clooney, and most importantly Michael B. articles.title: AI Movie ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Gets Serious with AI-Generated Grimes Cameo, Times Square Marketing Push, Oscar Screenings
articles.summary: Creator and YouTuber Gossip Goblin says it would be "disingenuous to write it all off" as just a stunt.
articles.content: When we first wrote about the coming release of “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the first fully AI-generated feature film being self-distributed into movie theaters in the U.S. , it would’ve been easy to write the whole thing off as a stunt. Coming from YouTuber Gossip Goblin , who has an impressive and loyal following, “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” started earning comps from the press (and from the producers themselves) to the success Markiplier found when he self-released his film “Iron Lung” and made $50 million worldwide in the process. Would that success translate for an AI movie? A recent example from China suggests that may not be the case. Related Stories Cannes 2026 Movies Sold: Kino Lorber Buys Clio Barnard’s BIFA Contender ‘I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning’ Sony Pictures Classics Buys Jean-Pierre Jeunet’s ‘Violette’ It’s clear though the team behind “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” is treating this like a real project that needs to be seen in theaters and is worthy of serious critical consideration, and they’re doing that with real marketing dollars behind its theatrical push. Today, Gossip Goblin announced that pop star Grimes is set to make a cameo in his film “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” as is YouTuber Mike Majlak, and their involvement is being revealed via a massive Times Square ad campaign that is also launching today, all ahead of the film’s release next month on December 4. Gossip Goblin is even launching a contest for people to use AI to create their own short films within the universe of “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” that can net the winning creator $15,000. “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” also sparked some headlines in the last few months with the news that the producers are plotting an Oscar campaign for Best Animated Feature. Turns out some FYC screenings have already started and a digital campaign begins at the end of November. All of the above suggests some real belief in the project, and with a collective 16 million views of the trailer thus far, they have reason to believe.
